question.problem:
A function $d(y)$ has values according to the table below:

| $y$ | $-5$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $d(y)$ | $-8.92$ | $-11.34$ | $-15.23$ | $-17.56$ | $-18.21$ | $-18.50$ |

Approximate ${d}^{′}(y)$ at the point $y=-5$ using a forward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

${d}^{′}(-5)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{d}^{′}(y)≈\frac{d(y+h)-d(y)}{h}
$$

at the point $y=-5.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}^{′}(-5) & ≈\frac{d(-5+2)-d(-5)}{2} \\  & =\frac{d(-3)-d(-5)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-11.34-(-8.92)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2.42}{2} \\  & =-1.21.\end{aligned}
$$
